rawCommits.subject: fix(evals): assert Stats via overflow menu and suppress onboarding modal
rawCommits.body:
The new Sessions/Terminal/Browser sidekick tabs push the last-positioned
Stats tab into the More overflow menu at the default panel width, so the
smoke + workflow evals can no longer find Stats as a top-level button.
Update both to open the More menu and assert the Stats menuitem instead.

The first-run welcome modal also overlays the app and intercepts clicks
(invisible to the old visibility-only asserts), so seed onboarding as
skipped/dismissed in both eval bootstraps to keep it from blocking evals.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: assert Stats via overflow menu and suppress onboarding modal

rawCommits.subject: fix(ios): add camera and photo library usage descriptions
rawCommits.body:
App Review rejected build 4231 (Guideline 2.1a) — tapping Take Photo
crashed with a TCC abort because Info.plist had no NSCameraUsageDescription.
The native image picker is reached from agent image selection
(accept=image/*) and message attachments (accept=*/*), both of which can
launch the camera and the photo library. Add NSCameraUsageDescription and
NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription so these flows prompt for permission instead
of crashing.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add camera and photo library usage descriptions

rawCommits.subject: feat(support): add public /support page for App Store Support URL
rawCommits.body:
App Review rejected build 4231 (Guideline 1.5) because the Support URL
(https://aura.ai/) had no support information. Add a standalone, ungated
/support route served by the aura.ai static site (the /* -> /index.html
rewrite resolves the deep link) so reviewers and users reach a page with a
support contact regardless of auth state. Set the App Store Connect Support
URL to https://aura.ai/support once support@aura.ai is live.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add public /support page for App Store Support URL

rawCommits.subject: feat(auth): add delete-account proxy to zOS (Apple 5.1.1v)
rawCommits.body:
Adds POST /api/auth/delete-account (protected) so the app can offer in-app
account deletion, required by App Store Guideline 5.1.1(v) now that the app
supports in-app account creation. This is a dormant backend endpoint — no UI
calls it yet.

The handler forwards the caller's JWT to zOS POST /api/v2/accounts/delete
(the same endpoint the ZERO mobile app uses), then tears down the local
session like logout. The upstream delete runs first so a failure leaves the
session intact and surfaces the error rather than claiming the account is
gone. zOS performs a soft delete that permanently blocks re-login.

Verified the route is registered and auth-guarded (401 without a token); the
destructive success path is not exercised in tests.

rawCommits.subject: feat(auth): wire deleteAccount in the interface auth store
rawCommits.body:
Adds authApi.deleteAccount() (POST /api/auth/delete-account) and a
deleteAccount store action. The action deletes upstream first and, unlike
logout, does NOT swallow errors: a failure propagates so the caller can
surface it and the local session stays intact. On success it reuses the
existing logout teardown, mirroring the ZERO mobile app which logs out after
a successful delete. Still no UI calls this yet.

Covered by unit tests for both the success and failure paths.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: wire deleteAccount in the interface auth store

rawCommits.subject: feat(settings): add native-only Delete Account flow (Apple 5.1.1v)
rawCommits.body:
Adds a Delete Account section at the bottom of the You settings pane, gated
to the native app via isNativeApp (the same gating credit purchases use). It
opens a confirmation modal whose copy makes the deletion permanent — matching
the ZERO mobile app — then calls the deleteAccount store action, which deletes
upstream and logs the user out on success.

Completes the in-app account-deletion requirement for iOS submission. Unit
tests cover native gating, the confirm flow, and the error path (zui Modal
stubbed per the codebase's modal-test convention); the real modal and the
full delete are verified on the TestFlight build.

rawCommits.subject: fix(mobile): make settings screens scrollable
rawCommits.body:
The mobile settings route root (.settingsRoot) had min-height:100% but no
overflow, so it was never a scroll viewport. Its parent .mobileMainPanel is
a bounded flex container with overflow:hidden, and the native shell sets
Capacitor scrollEnabled:false, so tall settings panes (e.g. You) were clipped
with no way to reach content below the fold.

Make .settingsRoot the scroll container (flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto),
mirroring the working ProjectStatsScreen/ProjectAgentsScreen route roots.

Scoped to the mobile-only CSS module (imported only by SettingsDetailScreen
and SettingsList); desktop renders settings via the separate SettingsView
component, so desktop and normal-width web are unaffected.

rawCommits.subject: feat(settings): add native-only Log Out button to You pane
rawCommits.body:
Mobile lacked an accessible logout (desktop/web have it via OrgSettingsPanel
and the profile, which aren't reachable in the mobile shell). Add a Log Out
row above Delete Account in the same isNativeApp-gated Account section, routed
through the canonical useLogout() hook (logout + navigate home).

Gated to native, so desktop and web are unchanged. Unit tests cover gating
and that Log Out invokes useLogout.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add native-only Log Out button to You pane

rawCommits.subject: feat(mobile): clearer prompt when a local agent is selected
rawCommits.body:
When a local agent is active the mobile chat input is disabled and showed
"Remote agent required". Expand it to "Remote agent required. Please switch
agent" so users (and App Review) know to go back and pick a remote agent, and
shrink just that placeholder so the longer text fits the narrow input (safe
below 16px since the field is disabled in this state).

Mobile-only: MobileChatInputBar and its scoped CSS class; desktop uses the
separate ChatInputBar.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: clearer prompt when a local agent is selected

rendered.title: Clearing the path to App Store approval
rendered.intro: Today's work is almost entirely focused on unblocking the iOS App Store submission for build 4231. The team shipped the missing pieces App Review flagged — camera and photo permissions, a public support page, in-app account deletion — alongside mobile polish (scrollable settings, a Log Out button, clearer chat guidance) and a fix to keep evals green as the sidekick UI evolves.

entries.title: Evals adapt to the new sidekick tab layout
entries.summary: End-to-end evals were updated to match the new Stats overflow behavior and to dismiss the first-run welcome modal that was silently intercepting clicks.

items.text: Smoke and workflow evals now open the More menu to assert the Stats menuitem, reflecting that new Sessions/Terminal/Browser sidekick tabs push Stats into the overflow at default panel width.
Both eval bootstraps now seed onboarding as skipped so the welcome modal no longer overlays the app and swallows clicks during runs.

entries.title: iOS camera and photo library permissions
entries.summary: Adds the Info.plist usage descriptions whose absence was crashing Take Photo on iOS and triggered an App Review rejection under Guideline 2.1a.

items.text: NSCameraUsageDescription and NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription are now declared, so agent image selection and message attachments prompt for permission instead of hitting a TCC abort.

entries.title: Public /support page for App Store reviewers
entries.summary: A standalone, ungated support page now lives at aura.ai/support to satisfy Guideline 1.5, accessible to reviewers and users regardless of auth state.

items.text: New SupportView is mounted as a top-level route outside AppShell and RequireAuth so the deep link resolves for logged-out visitors via the static site's SPA rewrite.
The page presents the Aura wordmark, a Support headline, and a contact email so App Store Connect's Support URL can point at it once support@aura.ai is live.

entries.title: Delete-account backend proxy to zOS
entries.summary: A new protected server endpoint forwards account-deletion requests upstream to zOS, laying the groundwork for the in-app deletion flow required by Apple 5.1.1(v).

items.text: POST /api/auth/delete-account is registered and auth-guarded, proxying the caller's JWT to zOS's accounts/delete and tearing down the local session only after the upstream delete succeeds so failures surface instead of silently orphaning state.

entries.title: Mobile account management lands in the You pane
entries.summary: The client side of the iOS-submission push: Delete Account and Log Out now live in the mobile You settings, the settings screen finally scrolls, and the local-agent chat prompt is clearer.

items.text: The auth store gained a deleteAccount action that calls the new backend, propagates errors so the UI can surface them, and only runs the logout teardown after a successful upstream delete.
A native-only Delete Account section with a permanent-deletion confirmation modal now sits at the bottom of the You pane, completing the in-app deletion requirement for iOS submission.
A native-only Log Out row sits above Delete Account, giving mobile users an accessible sign-out that desktop already had via OrgSettingsPanel.
Mobile settings screens are now their own scroll viewport, so tall panes like You are reachable below the fold instead of being clipped by the bounded native shell.

The disabled mobile chat input now reads "Remote agent required. Please switch agent" — with a smaller placeholder so the longer guidance fits — making the next step explicit for users and App Review when a local agent is selected.

highlights: iOS in-app account deletion shipped end-to-end (Apple 5.1.1v)
Camera and photo library permissions added to unblock Take Photo
Public /support page live for App Store Guideline 1.5
Mobile settings now scroll and expose Log Out
